blocks.text: I can explain what is shown by a food web diagram and explain the effects that a change in the size of a population could have on other populations in the same community.

items.title: Population changes impact a food web

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. It must provide food, shelter and a place to reproduce.
A group of organisms of the same type in the same place is called a population.
A community is made up of all the organisms that live in the same place.
A food chain diagram shows how food is transferred from one population of organisms to another.
A food web diagram shows how all food chains interact with each other.

blocks.text: The place where an organism lives is called its habitat. A habitat has to provide three things:
The largest habitat is the ocean. Habitats can be much smaller too, for example under logs or leaves in a woodland. Very small habitats are called **microhabitats**.
All of the different organisms that live in the same place form a **community**. A community is a group of populations.
A coral reef habitat has a community of different populations of fish and different types of coral.

items: In an Arctic habitat, organisms have to be adapted to keep warm.
In an ocean habitat, organisms have to be adapted to live in salty water.

blocks.text: There are lots of interactions in a community.

items.title: Helping with jobs like cleaning
items.sub: an oxpecker cleaning parasites from a buffalo

items.title: Feeding relationships
items.sub: a heron catching and eating a fish

items.q: Which of these is a population?
options: All the daisies in a field
All the different organisms in a pond

items.q: Which of these is a community?
options: All the different organisms that live in a pond

items.q: A habitat has to provide food, shelter and…

slides.title: Why a food chain is too simple

blocks.text: Communities are made up of lots of food chains, and most consumers eat more than one type of food. A food chain shows just one feeding relationship.

items: oak leaf → aphid → ladybird → blue tit → wildcat

blocks.text: Each organism in this chain could also be eaten by consumers that are not shown.
A {food web} diagram is a set of linked food chains. It is a better model, because feeding relationships are often complex.
Here are four food chains from a woodland:

items: oak leaves → snail → hedgehog → fox
oak leaves → earthworm → hedgehog → fox
oak leaves → vole → weasel → fox
oak leaves → vole → owl

blocks.label: Link them together
blocks.text: All four chains start with oak leaves, so they share a producer. The vole is in two chains, and the hedgehog and the fox appear in more than one chain. Joined together, they make a food web.

blocks.q: Why is a food web a better model than a food chain?
options: It shows that producers and primary consumers are usually eaten by more than one organism in the habitat
It shows that there are more producers than consumers in a habitat
blocks.why: Many producers and primary consumers are eaten by more than one population, and a food web shows this. A food chain shows just one simple feeding relationship.

blocks.text: This garden food web is made up of five food chains:

items: cabbage → caterpillar → chaffinch → cat
cabbage → caterpillar → thrush → cat
lavender → caterpillar → chaffinch → cat
lavender → caterpillar → thrush → cat
lavender → bee → thrush → cat

blocks.text: Caterpillars eat cabbage. Thrushes eat caterpillars and bees. The chaffinch and the thrush are both predators and prey.
Use the five food chains on the last slide.

items.q: How many of the food chains start with lavender?
Which organism is eaten by the thrush but not by the chaffinch?
Which two organisms are food for the cat?
Which organism is the apex predator?

items: lettuce → snail → thrush → hawk

blocks.text: A change to one population can have a large effect on the others. If the number of **thrushes decreases**:

items: the snail population increases, because there are fewer thrushes to eat them
the lettuce population decreases, because more snails eat them
the hawk population decreases, because there are fewer thrushes to eat

blocks.text: Food webs show more complex feeding relationships. In a woodland food web, imagine the population of **thrushes decreases**:

items: Foxes will eat more mice and rabbits.
Buzzards will eat more mice, rabbits and snails.
Fewer worms will be eaten, so the worm population will increase.
The rabbit and mouse populations will decrease, so the grass and wild flowers will not be eaten so much and their populations will increase.

blocks.text: Removing just one organism from a food web can have many effects, because the organism can be in several food chains.
Take one food chain from the garden: lavender → bee → thrush → cat. What if the cats are taken away?

blocks.label: Thrushes
blocks.text: The thrush population will increase, because the thrushes are not being eaten by the cat.

blocks.label: Bees
blocks.text: The thrushes, now more in number, will eat more bees, so the bee population will decrease.

blocks.label: Lavender
blocks.text: Bees are important for lavender to pollinate. Without the bees, the lavender will find it harder to reproduce, so the number of lavender plants may decrease.
Introducing organisms can be dangerous too.

items: Ground nesting birds were common in New Zealand, because there were very few predators that ate their eggs.
Rats were introduced to New Zealand in the late 1700s. They ate the eggs as food, and their population increased quickly.
As more rats ate more eggs, the bird populations declined. Many ground nesting birds are now endangered because of the rats.

items.q: In lavender → bee → thrush → cat, the number of thrushes falls. What happens to the bee population?
options: It increases, because fewer bees are eaten
It decreases, because bees eat thrushes

items.q: A change in the size of one population only affects organisms in the same food chain. True or false?
options: False: it can affect other populations in the food web too

items.q: Why can removing one organism from a food web have many effects?
options: It can be in several food chains
It is always the largest organism

items: A community is made up of all the different organisms that live in a habitat.
Interactions take place between different organisms in a community, including feeding relationships.
Food web diagrams are models that give a more realistic picture of feeding relationships in a habitat.
Changes in the populations of organisms affect all the organisms in a food chain. They also affect other populations in the food web, because a food web is made up of connecting food chains.

flashcards.back: The place where an organism lives. It must provide food, shelter and a place to reproduce.

flashcards.front: What three things must a habitat provide?
flashcards.back: Food, shelter and a place to reproduce.
A very small habitat, for example under logs or leaves in a woodland.
All the organisms that live in the same place. It is a group of populations.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a population and a community?
flashcards.back: A population is organisms of one type in one place. A community is all the different populations that live in the same place.

flashcards.front: Give an example of organisms helping each other in a community.
flashcards.back:
A bee pollinating a crocus.

Or an oxpecker cleaning parasites from a buffalo.
A set of linked food chains. It shows how all food chains interact with each other.

flashcards.front: Why is a food chain too simple a model?
flashcards.back: It shows just one feeding relationship, but most consumers eat more than one type of food.

flashcards.front: Why is a food web a better model than a food chain?
flashcards.back: It gives a more realistic picture of feeding relationships, showing that organisms can feed on more than one other organism.

flashcards.front: Why can removing one organism from a food web have many effects?
flashcards.back: The organism can be in several food chains, so other populations can be affected.

flashcards.front: If cats are removed from lavender → bee → thrush → cat, what happens to the thrush population?
flashcards.back: It increases, because the thrushes are no longer eaten by the cat.

flashcards.front: What happened to ground nesting birds in New Zealand after rats were introduced?
flashcards.back: The rats ate their eggs, so the bird populations declined and many are now endangered.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Food webs
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: Habitats provide organisms with food, shelter and a place to do what? (Answer in one word.)
questions.explanation: A habitat must provide food, shelter and a place to reproduce.

questions.prompt: What is the name for all the organisms that live in the same place?
questions.explanation: A community is made up of all the organisms that live in the same place.

questions.prompt: What is the name for very small habitats, such as under a log?
questions.explanation: Very small habitats are called microhabitats.
The largest habitat is the ocean.

questions.prompt: A food web is a set of linked what? (Answer in two words.)
questions.explanation: A food web diagram is a set of linked food chains.

questions.prompt: In the food chain cabbage → caterpillar → chaffinch → cat, which organism is the apex predator?
questions.explanation: The cat is at the end of the chain and is not prey for any other organism in it.

questions.prompt: In lavender → bee → thrush → cat, the cats are removed. Does the thrush population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: The thrushes are no longer being eaten by the cat.

questions.prompt: In lavender → bee → thrush → cat, the cats are removed and the thrush population grows. Does the bee population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: The thrushes, now more in number, eat more bees.

questions.prompt: In a woodland food web, the population of thrushes decreases, so fewer worms are eaten. Does the worm population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: Fewer worms are eaten, so their population increases.
